subject: PO formatting, phased invoicing & net-term constraints from procurement
messages:
From: Elena Morales <emorales@grandehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@grandehealth.com; ap@grandehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RE: PO formatting, phased invoicing & net-term constraints from procurement

Hi Vanessa / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has a few constraints we need clarified before we can issue a PO:

1) PO numbering format: our ERP requires a single PO per fiscal project but we can accept multiple invoice lines per PO. Is Redwood able to accept the PO number in the header and on each invoice line?

2) Invoice cadence: budget reconciliation prefers monthly statements, but payments are run quarterly. Can invoices be produced monthly with a quarter-end consolidated statement?

3) Net terms: standard for our org is Net 60 after receipt; however, AP is open to Net 45 for first-year pilots if a 2% early-payment discount is provided for Net 30. Is a conditional discount available?

4) Advance/retainer: Can Redwood accept a split billing schedule (20% retainer up-front, then monthly consumption invoices)? If so, we will need an SOW that shows the breakdown for our finance system.

I attached our PO template for reference (Grande_Health_PO_Template.pdf). Please let me know what you need and we can route internally.

Best,
Elena
Senior Procurement Manager
Grande Health

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <emorales@grandehealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai; procurement@grandehealth.com; ap@grandehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-16T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: RE: PO formatting, phased invoicing & net-term constraints from procurement

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers from pricing/sales side:

- PO number: yes, we can include the PO number in the invoice header and on each invoice line — our billing system supports a single PO with multiple invoices attached.

- Monthly invoices + quarterly payment run: we can issue invoices monthly and provide a consolidated quarterly statement that lists all monthly invoices and totals for your AP team.

- Net terms / early-payment discount: We typically publish Net 30 for self-serve and Net 45 for committed contracts. Net 60 is longer than our standard for enterprise pilots. For a first-year pilot we can agree to Net 60 if the customer is on an annual commitment and pays a 10% prepayment/retainer. Alternatively, we can offer a 1.5% early-payment discount for Net 30 on invoices paid within 14 days — this is negotiable with finance.

- Split billing / retainer: Yes — we can structure a 20% retainer and monthly consumption invoices. We'll need the SOW breakdown and the PO to map billable line items properly.

I'll loop in Marissa from Finance to propose the formal terms and draft invoice examples.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <emorales@grandehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai; vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai; procurement@grandehealth.com; ap@grandehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-16T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: RE: PO formatting, phased invoicing & net-term constraints from procurement

Elena —

Thanks; adding the finance perspective and a proposed billing model. High-level constraints from our side:

- PO mapping: We need the PO number, the invoice-to legal entity, and the cost center code on the PO. If Grande Health requires specific GL codes on invoice line items, include those in the PO PDF or the SOW so our billing team can populate them.

- Invoice cadence: We can issue monthly invoices and also generate a consolidated quarterly statement PDF with a summary page and individual invoice pages attached. That works for your quarterly payment runs.

- Net terms / discounts: Our standard enterprise net terms are Net 45. For Net 60 we require one of the following: 1) a 10% annual prepayment, or 2) a signed purchase order that includes milestone-based statements with guaranteed payment windows (we will also require credit approval). We can offer a 1.5% discount for invoices paid within 14 days (Net 14 discount) up to $250k annual spend; for larger commitments we can scale the discount — happy to include specific language in the SOW/contract.

- Retainer / split invoicing: We'll accept a 20% retainer to be invoiced on PO receipt and then monthly consumption invoices. The retainer will apply as a credit against the final monthly invoice.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Elena — please confirm the required PO fields (cost center, GL code, ERP header format).
2) Elena — confirm whether Grande Health will sign an annual commitment or treat this as a pilot (this affects Net-60 eligibility).
3) Ben / Vanessa / Marissa — we'll produce a sample invoice set (retainer invoice + two monthly invoices + quarterly consolidated statement) and a contract addendum showing the early-payment discount language.

I'll attach a sample SOW template showing billing line items.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: SOW-Redwood-Inference-GrandeHealth-v1.2.docx (shows line-item mapping and GL code fields)

From: Elena Morales <emorales@grandehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai; vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@grandehealth.com; ap@grandehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-17T08:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PO formatting, phased invoicing & net-term constraints from procurement

Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the quick responses and detail. A few clarifications from our AP team after reviewing:

- Cost center / GL: We can include cost center and GL codes on the PO header and on each invoice line. We will provide the exact codes in the PO.

- Commitment: For the pilot we are not ready to sign an annual commitment. This will be a 6-month pilot with the option to scale to an annual agreement afterward. Because it's a pilot, Finance prefers Net 60 without prepayment; however, AP can move to Net 45 if Redwood will accept a 0.75% early-pay discount for payments within 14 days.

- Retainer: We can do the 20% retainer upon PO issuance. Will Redwood accept that as a credit and apply it to the first invoice?

- PO sequencing: Our ERP can accept one PO with multiple invoice references (we will provide the header and the per-invoice reference format). Please confirm the acceptable invoice reference format (e.g. PO-12345/INV-202611).

If you can confirm the points above, I will route the PO to our director for signature.

Best,
Elena

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <emorales@grandehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai; procurement@grandehealth.com; ap@grandehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-18T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: PO formatting, phased invoicing & net-term constraints from procurement

Elena —

Thanks — we are aligned and can accept the pilot terms with the adjustments below. Confirm back and we'll ask our contracts team to prepare the PO-attachment and addendum.

1) Invoice referencing: acceptable format = PO-<number>/INV-<YYYYMM>-<seq> (example: PO-98765/INV-202611-01). Our billing will include the PO header and the invoice reference on each invoice line.

2) Retainer: 20% retainer invoice upon PO receipt — applied as credit to first invoice. That will be a separate invoice (INV-202611-01) referencing the PO number.

3) Net terms / discount: For a 6-month pilot we will accept Net 60 without prepayment. Alternatively, if Grande Health prefers Net 45, we will apply a 0.75% early-pay discount for payments made within 14 days (Net 14 discount). Please indicate which path you prefer.

4) GL/cost center fields: we can populate GL and cost center fields on each invoice line if you include them in the PO. Please include those codes in the PO header or an attached mapping table.

Next steps:
- Elena: confirm Net 60 (no prepay) OR Net 45 + 0.75% early-pay discount; provide PO with cost center/GL codes.
- Once confirmed, Contracts will prepare a short addendum and we'll send 20% retainer invoice upon PO receipt.

I'll put the addendum draft in DocuSign and share a preview link when ready.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
